intro: Convert grains (gr) into grams (g, or grammes) accurately for ammunition reloading, archery arrow weights, precious metals, and apothecary scales. Based on the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement, each grain to gram conversion uses the exact ratio 1 grain = 0.06479891 grams (1/7,000 pound), while 1 gram equals 15.43236 grains. Check standard grains grams bullet and arrow weights from 1 gr to 1,000 gr below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Grains (gr) vs. Grams (g) & Troy vs. Avoirdupois Consistency
items: Never mix up the abbreviation 'gr' (grain = 0.0648 g) with 'g' (gram = 15.43236 gr): treating grains as grams in powder reloading or pharmaceutical dosing produces a 15.4× error.

The international grain (64.79891 mg) is identical across avoirdupois, troy, and apothecaries' systems—only the number of grains per pound differs (7,000 gr per avoirdupois lb vs. 5,760 gr per troy lb).

faqs.question: How many grams are in 1 grain?
faqs.answer: There are 0.06479891 grams (about 0.0648 g or 64.8 mg) in 1 grain. Conversely, 1 gram equals 15.43236 grains.

faqs.question: How do I convert grains to grams?
faqs.answer: Multiply the weight in grains by 0.06479891 (or divide by 15.4323584): g = gr × 0.06479891. For example, 100 grains × 0.06479891 = 6.47989 grams.

faqs.question: Is a grain the same in troy and avoirdupois weight?
faqs.answer: Yes—under the international standard, 1 grain is identical in both systems at 0.06479891 grams (64.79891 mg). An avoirdupois pound has 7,000 grains, while a troy pound has 5,760 grains.
